title: Finding Issues: List, Filters & Search
subtitle: Narrow the list, search every word (including notes), save the views you use most, and jump anywhere from the keyboard.
in_this_chapter: The issue list and what each column shows
Every filter control, and the values each one offers
Full-text search — and why it finds more than you'd expect
Saving filters and sharing them by link
Plain-English (AI) search, when it's turned on

callout.label: QUICK VERSION
callout.text: Click **Issues** in the left navigation, set any mix of filters (project, status, severity, priority, tag, or a text search), and click **Search**. Save a filter you use often so it becomes a one-click pill, or press **Ctrl+K** (**Cmd+K** on a Mac) to jump anywhere without the mouse.

blocks.p: Select **Issues** in the left navigation to open the issue list. It shows every issue you're allowed to view, across all your projects at once — the place most day-to-day finding happens. A **filter bar** runs along the top; the results appear as a table below it, and a small line reads how many matched, for example __24 issue(s) match__. If nothing matches, it reads __No issues match this filter.__
Each row in the results table shows, left to right:

rows: The issue's number — its permanent ID. Handy for the command palette and for linking relationships.
**Project**
Which project the issue belongs to.
**Title**
The issue's title, as a link. Click it to open the full issue.
**Status**
Where the issue is in its lifecycle (New, Assigned, Resolved, and so on).
**Severity**
How serious the issue is (Minor, Major, Crash, and so on).
**Priority**
How urgently it should be handled (Low, Normal, High, and so on).
**Assignee**
Who it's assigned to, or __Unassigned__.
**Updated**
When the issue last changed.

blocks.screenshot: The issue list: the filter bar across the top, the saved-filter pills, and the results table below

blocks.p: The filter bar is a row of drop-downs and boxes. You set any combination of them and click **Search** — the filters **combine**, so each one you add narrows the results further (project __Website__ *and* status __Assigned__ *and* severity __Crash__ returns only issues matching all three). Leaving a control on its __Any__ or __All__ setting means "don't filter on this." The controls are:

rows: **Project**
__All projects__, or any one project you can see.
Limits the list to a single project.
**Status**
__Any__, New, Feedback, Acknowledged, Confirmed, Assigned, Resolved, Closed.
Shows only issues in the chosen lifecycle state.
**Severity**
__Any__, Feature, Trivial, Text, Tweak, Minor, Major, Crash, Block.
Shows only issues of the chosen seriousness.
**Priority**
__Any__, None, Low, Normal, High, Urgent, Immediate.
Shows only issues at the chosen urgency.
**Tag**
__Any__, or any tag in use across the instance.
Shows only issues carrying that tag — the payoff of tagging consistently.
**Text**
A free-text box.
Full-text search across title, description, and notes (see below).

blocks.p: Two buttons finish the bar: **Search** applies whatever you've set, and **Clear** wipes every filter and returns the list to its default, unfiltered state.

callout.label: YOU ONLY EVER SEE WHAT YOU'RE ALLOWED TO
callout.text: Filtering can only ever narrow what you already have permission to view. Your access is applied first, then your filters on top. So a text search or a shared filter link can never surface an issue in a project you don't have access to.

blocks.p: The **Sort by** drop-down (at the right of the filter bar) sets the order of the results. Your choices are:

bullets: **Updated (newest)** — most recently changed first. This is the usual default.
**Created (newest)** and **Created (oldest)** — by when the issue was first filed.

blocks.p: Next to the sort control is a checkbox: **Stale only (open, 30+ days idle)**. Tick it to show just the open issues that nobody has touched in over 30 days — your "what's been forgotten?" view. It's the fastest way to surface work that quietly stalled. Combine it with a project or severity filter to focus the cleanup.

callout.label: SET YOUR OWN DEFAULT SORT
callout.text: If you didn't pick a sort, the list uses your preferred default order (set in your preferences), falling back to __Updated (newest)__ if you haven't chosen one. Pick a sort here any time to override it for the current search.

blocks.h1: Full-text search — it looks inside the notes, too

blocks.p: The **Text** box does more than match titles. It searches an issue's **title, its description, and every note on it**. That last part matters: a detail someone mentioned only in a comment three weeks ago will still surface the issue, even if that word appears nowhere in the title or description. You don't have to remember *where* something was written — only that it was.

callout.label: SEARCH IS CASE-INSENSITIVE AND PARTIAL
callout.text: Matching ignores capitalization and matches on part of a word, so __login__ finds __Login__ and __logins__. When a search returns too much, add a filter (a project, a status, or a tag) rather than a longer phrase — the filters and the text box work together.

blocks.h1: Save a filter, and share it

blocks.p: Built a filter combination you'll want again? Don't rebuild it by hand each time — save it. Saved filters appear as one-click **pills** in a row just above the results.

steps: Set up the filter exactly as you want it (any mix of drop-downs, the text box, sort, and the stale toggle).
In the box labeled __Save current filter as…__, type a name for it.
Click **Save**. The filter becomes a pill above the list; click that pill any time to re-run the whole filter in one click.
To remove a saved filter, use the **Delete a saved filter…** drop-down next to the save box, pick it, and click **Delete**.

callout.label: BOOKMARK OR SHARE ANY VIEW BY LINK
callout.text: Every filter is written into the page's web address (URL). Whenever you run a search, the address bar updates to match — so you can **bookmark** that view in your browser, or **paste the link** to a colleague and they'll open the very same filtered list. (They'll still only see the issues they're allowed to, so a shared link never leaks anything.)

blocks.screenshot: The saved-filter row: existing filter pills, the Save current filter as box, and the Delete a saved filter drop-down

blocks.h1: Plain-English search (when AI is turned on)

blocks.p: If your OpenTrack administrator has turned on the optional AI features, an extra box appears above the filter bar labeled **✨ Ask in plain English**. Type a request the way you'd say it out loud — for example, __high-priority crashes nobody has touched in a month__ — and click **Search with AI**. OpenTrack turns your sentence into the ordinary filters below (status, severity, priority, keywords, stale, project) and runs them. You can then tweak those filters by hand and search again.

callout.label: IT ONLY FILLS IN THE FILTERS
callout.text: Plain-English search can only ever produce a filter you could have built yourself with the controls above — it adds no hidden search power and can't reach issues you're not permitted to see. If it can't make sense of your request, it says so; try naming a status, severity, priority, keyword, or "stale." If AI is switched off for your instance, this box simply isn't there.

blocks.p: For fast, mouse-free navigation, OpenTrack has a **command palette** — a quick-jump box you can pop open from any page. It only ever navigates (it changes which page you're on); it never changes data, so it's completely safe to open and poke around in.

steps: Press **Ctrl + K** (on a Mac, **Cmd + K**). A search box drops down over the middle of the screen, prompting __Type to search, #123 to jump to an issue, or a command…__.
Start typing. The list below the box updates as you type.
Use the **↓** and **↑** arrow keys to move the highlight through the matches (the top one is highlighted to start).
Press **Enter** to go to the highlighted match — or click any match with the mouse.
Press **Esc**, or click outside the box, to close it without going anywhere.

blocks.p: What you can type into it:

rows: A number like `142` or `#142`
A __Go to issue #142__ result that opens that issue directly.
A word or phrase
Matching **commands** (see below), plus a __Search issues for "…"__ result that runs a text search for what you typed.
Part of a command name
That command — for example typing __back__ finds __Backup & export__.

blocks.p: The built-in commands the palette can jump to are: **Dashboard**, **All issues**, **Quick add a problem** (the fast issue-reporting form), **Projects**, **Notifications**, and **Backup & export**.

blocks.screenshot: The command palette open over the page, showing the search box and a list of quick matches including Go to issue and command entries

bullets: __My search returns nothing.__ A leftover filter is probably too tight. Click **Clear** to reset everything, then add filters back one at a time. Remember the filters combine — project *and* status *and* severity all have to match at once.

__An issue I expected isn't in the list.__ Check the **Project** filter isn't pinned to the wrong project, that **Status** isn't hiding it (a Closed issue won't show if Status is set to New), and that **Stale only** isn't ticked. If you still can't see it, you may not have access to its project.

__My text search isn't finding a word I know is there.__ The Text box matches title, description, and notes — but not attachments' contents. If the word only lives inside an attached file, search won't find it. Otherwise, check for a typo and remember matching ignores capitalization.

__I saved a filter but it's not in the pills.__ Give the filter a name in the __Save current filter as…__ box before clicking **Save** — an unnamed filter isn't saved. Then look for its pill in the row above the results.

__I pasted a filter link to a colleague and they see fewer issues.__ That's expected: a shared filter link shows each person only the issues they're allowed to view. The filter is the same; the access is theirs.

__The ✨ Ask in plain English box isn't there.__ AI features are optional and off unless an administrator enables them. Use the regular filter bar instead — it can do everything the plain-English box turns your request into.

__Ctrl+K does nothing.__ Make sure the OpenTrack page has focus (click once on the page first). On a Mac use **Cmd+K**. If a browser extension has claimed that shortcut, you can still open any page from the left navigation instead.
